title: B1: lone pairs and hydrogens compared with RDKit
truth: RDKit 2026.09.1 (@rdkit/rdkit 2026.9.1): implicit hydrogens; lone pairs implied by its valence model

chembl.SEED: 20261106 (molecules in the order of a hash of the seed and the ChEMBL ID; see make-chembl-samples.mjs)
chembl.FILTER: largest fragment (salts split); only H B C N O F Si P S Cl Se Br I; RDKit reads it; at most 100 heavy atoms
chembl.COLUMNS: chembl_id, SMILES (ChEMBL canonical SMILES of the largest fragment), tab separated

hard.SOURCE: written for this benchmark (textbook species); extends the molecules in tests/chem.test.mjs

cases.name: alanate
cases.reason: Al1 has 0 H here, RDKit 4; 2 lone pairs here, RDKit 0
cases.explanation: olomol gives Al no implicit hydrogens (it is not in the VALENCES table of src/chem/elements.js: 'other elements only have the hydrogens drawn or set'). RDKit gives Al valence 3. So a hand-drawn Al with too few bonds shows no H, and AlH4⁻ drawn as Al⁻ even shows two lone pairs. Read as a pasted SMILES, the molfile's hydrogen count is kept and olomol agrees with RDKit.

cases.name: chlorine-atom
cases.explanation: RDKit's molfile gives the chlorine atom no RAD line, only valence 0 in the atom line. With that count dropped (the 'rules' mode) the file holds a plain Cl, and olomol's rules give HCl. Read as a pasted SMILES (the molfile as it is), olomol gives 0 H and 3 lone pairs, as RDKit does. Drawn in olomol, the radical tool sets the unpaired electron and the counts are right (methyl and hydroxyl radicals agree).
